family.tagline: One Companion Core, one kitchen whiteboard, and two teens sharing a room.
family.story: Sally runs a small consultancy from the craft room, and John writes software at the garage workbench. Steve claims the den downstairs, and Jean studies at the desk in the room she shares with him. One Companion Core stands in the kitchen, beside the whiteboard.

home.lede: A mid-century raised ranch with a garage tucked under it, between fieldstone piers. The main floor sits a storey up, behind a brick-walled loggia. Stepping stones cross a lavender garden to the stoop.

spots.line: A whiteboard on the wall, the Core beside it, and a glass table.
A standing desk, an easel and two ladder shelves.
A workbench, a bicycle and a wheelbarrow.
A sofa, two barrel chairs, the TV and a drum kit.
Two single beds, one desk and a rocking horse.

day.line: Monday starts with Friday's calls and a fresh to-do list.
John opens the cut list at the workbench.
At lunch the family reads the week off the whiteboard.
The month's invoices go out before the weekend.
Jean writes up her French test at the glass table.
Steve starts a session in the den.
Jean takes the August picture from the stepping stone.

members.name: Sally
members.work: consultant, runs her own small practice

companion.name: Juniper
companion.job: Drafts replies and proposals for Sally's clients from the context she connected.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Sally reads and sends every message.

profile.bio: Sally runs a small consultancy from the craft room. Her call notes, client sign-ins and invoices sit on the Core, and Juniper drafts replies that she reads before she sends them.

companion.name: Quill
companion.job: Opens supplier order forms and fills in the details John typed.
companion.limits: One form at a time. John reads each field and sends it himself.

profile.bio: John writes software and builds shelves in the garage. His code sits in Gitea on the Core, and Quill fills in the order forms that he checks and sends himself.
Steve plays on the den TV, drums in the same room and shares a bedroom with his sister. His headphones keep that room quiet for her.
Jean studies at the desk she shares with her brother. She keeps a note for every French test, draws her maths in a browser and reads her set text, with tools that each do one job on the Core.

popup.title: A parcel halfway up the steps
popup.body: The courier leaves a parcel on the stoop landing, halfway up the steps. John carries it up to the loggia and through the living room to the kitchen.

popup.title: Four things in the parcel
popup.body: Steve cuts the tape. Jean lifts out the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. She reads the guide aloud.

popup.title: Plugged in beside the whiteboard
popup.body: Sally plugs the cable in by the whiteboard. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from John's phone
popup.body: John joins the Core's own network from his phone, then picks the home network.

popup.title: Sally and John choose their agents
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Sally picks Hermes and John picks OpenClaw. Companion Memory comes along, with Yuvomi, Joplin Server and Gitea. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Juniper says hello
popup.body: Sally messages the agent she named Juniper. The reply comes from the Core, a floor above her craft room.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: sally
say.text: Hello, Sally. I am Juniper. What should we start with?

detail.before: Without an agent, Sally wrote every reply and reminder herself, one app at a time.
detail.after: Juniper runs in a sandbox on the Core and replies through the messaging app Sally picked. Those messages travel through that chat service.
steps: Pick Hermes in the Companion Hub store
Give the agent a name
Send it a first message
detail.fact: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals and notes

popup.title: Thursday survives the sleeve
popup.body: A sleeve wipes Thursday off the whiteboard. Its twin in Yuvomi on the Core still has the dentist and the dinner.

detail.before: The week lived on the whiteboard and, copied by hand, in a calendar service on each phone. When they disagreed, nobody knew which was right.
detail.after: Yuvomi keeps the calendar, tasks, shopping and meals in a database on the Core. The whiteboard stays on the wall as the copy everyone reads.
steps: Copy Sunday's whiteboard into Yuvomi
Add the dinners and the shopping list
Read Thursday back when the board is wiped
detail.fact: Yuvomi is a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals and notes, stored in SQLite on your Core.

beats.capability: archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them

popup.title: The range hood hums its last
popup.body: When the range hood stops humming, the warranty is in Papra, added from the old Drive folder. The family's receipts, warranties and contracts are archived there, on the Core.

detail.before: Receipts went into one Google Drive folder called house, and the range hood's warranty was somewhere among the photos.
detail.after: Papra archives each receipt, warranty and contract on the Core, so the one the family needs is there when the hood stops.
steps: Add the receipt to Papra
File it with the warranty
Open it when the hood stops
detail.fact: Papra archives the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them.

beats.capability: capture quick notes and journal entries in Markdown

popup.title: A note for every vocab test
popup.body: At the glass table, Jean writes a note for each French test, with the words she missed. Memos keeps them as Markdown on the Core, not in a notes service.

detail.before: Jean's missed words went into Google Keep, in one pile with every other quick note.
detail.after: Memos keeps one note for each test on the Core, in Markdown. Jean reads back through them before the next test.
steps: Write down the words she missed
Save the note for that test
Read the old notes before the next one
detail.fact: Memos captures quick notes and journal entries in Markdown.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: The homework site comes back
popup.body: Jean's vocabulary site stops loading on the sofa. John adds it to the Pi-hole allow list, and the page opens.
popup.note: Lookups it does not block still go to the DNS provider the family picked.

detail.before: NextDNS answered the house's DNS lookups, and the allow list lived in its settings.
detail.after: Pi-hole answers the house's DNS on the Core. John keeps the allow list there and adds a site when the family needs a page back.
steps: Find the blocked site
Add it to the allow list
Reload the page on the sofa
detail.fact: Pi-hole blocks ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Headphones on, the shared room quiet
popup.body: Steve streams the albums the family owns from the Core to his phone. His headphones keep the room quiet for Jean. Navidrome plays only the files the family holds.

detail.before: Steve played his music through Spotify on his phone.
detail.after: Navidrome streams the family's music files from the Core to his phone over the home Wi-Fi.
steps: Open Navidrome on the phone
Pick a folder of the family's music
Put the headphones on
detail.fact: Navidrome streams your own music collection to any device.

beats.capability: send files between phones and laptops on the same Wi-Fi

popup.title: Three paces from bed to desk
popup.body: Jean's school concert video is too big for the family chat. Steve sends it past the old rocking horse with PairDrop, served by the Core, over the home Wi-Fi.

detail.before: Steve's phone and Jean's school laptop are different makes, so a video too big for the family chat went by cable.
detail.after: PairDrop sends the file straight from Steve's phone to Jean's laptop over the home Wi-Fi, with no chat app between.
steps: Open PairDrop on the phone and the laptop
Choose the laptop from the phone
Send the video across the room
detail.fact: PairDrop sends files between phones and laptops on the same Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: draw flowcharts, floor plans and network maps in the browser

popup.title: The shared room, drawn to scale
popup.body: Jean measures her shared room for a maths scale drawing. draw.io opens from the Core, and she draws the beds, the desk and the shelf.

detail.before: Jean's diagrams for school were drawn in Lucidchart.
detail.after: draw.io opens in her browser from the Core. Jean draws the two beds, the desk and the shelf to scale.
steps: Measure the beds, the desk and the shelf
Draw the plan to scale in draw.io
Check the drawing against the room
detail.fact: draw.io draws flowcharts, floor plans and network maps in the browser.

beats.capability: a searchable catalog of local-AI and self-hosting tools

popup.title: Three names for John
popup.body: Jean searches Spellbook on the Core for a computing club project. She copies three tool names onto a card for John to read at dinner.
popup.note: Crash reports go to Companion Intelligence unless switched off.

detail.before: A project idea meant a search engine, a dozen open tabs and no list to hand John.
detail.after: Spellbook is a searchable catalog on the Core. Jean reads three entries and copies the names for John.
steps: Search the catalog for a topic
Read three entries
Copy the names onto a card for John
detail.fact: Spellbook is a searchable catalog of local-AI and self-hosting tools.

beats.capability: read ebooks in your browser, with notes, highlights and text-to-speech

popup.title: The set text joins the library
popup.body: The school sends the set text as a file. Jean keeps it in a Koodo Reader library on the Core. She reads it on the beanbag by the shelf.
popup.note: It opens the family's own ebook files.

detail.before: Jean read her set texts in Apple Books, with her notes kept in that app.
detail.after: Koodo Reader opens the school's file in a browser, from a library on the Core. Jean highlights the lines she wants in the same app.
steps: Put the school's file in the library
Open it in Koodo Reader
Highlight the lines she wants
detail.fact: Koodo Reader reads ebooks in your browser, with notes, highlights and text-to-speech, and keeps the library on your Core.

beats.capability: take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server

popup.title: Last week's calls, this week's list
popup.body: Sally has moved four years of client notes into Joplin Server on the Core. At the standing desk on Monday, she turns Friday's calls into the week's to-do list.
popup.note: Joplin Server is the server. The Joplin apps are separate.

detail.before: Four years of call notes sat in Evernote, one notebook per client, and the to-do list lived somewhere else.
detail.after: Joplin Server syncs the notes and the to-do list between her laptop and her phone, through the server on the Core.
steps: Open Friday's call notes
Turn each action into a to-do
Check the list on her phone
detail.fact: Joplin Server lets you take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server.

beats.capability: keeps your digital life on your own disk and gives your agents individual context

popup.title: Juniper drafts the renewal, Sally checks
popup.body: Juniper drafts a renewal reply from last spring's thread, which Sally connected to Companion Memory. Sally checks the figures, then sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

detail.before: A renewal reply meant digging out last spring's thread and rebuilding the figures by hand.
detail.after: Juniper drafts the reply on the Core from the thread Sally connected in Companion Memory. She checks every figure, then sends it herself.
steps: Ask Juniper for the renewal reply
Check each figure against the thread
Send the reply herself
detail.fact: Companion Memory keeps your digital life on your disk, so your agents know your context.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host that works with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: The old account closes last
popup.body: Before Sally closes her old password account, she opens every client sign-in from the new vault. VaultWarden runs on the Core and works with the Bitwarden apps.

detail.before: Client portal sign-ins lived in LastPass, and the family's shared ones sat on a sticky note by the whiteboard.
detail.after: VaultWarden keeps the sign-ins in a vault on the Core. Sally opens them with the Bitwarden apps, and the sticky note goes in the bin.
steps: Open each client sign-in from VaultWarden
Check that every one works
Close the old account
detail.fact: VaultWarden stores every password in a vault you host and works with the Bitwarden apps.

beats.capability: send invoices and quotes, track expenses and time

popup.title: Invoice day reuses an old quote
popup.body: On the last Friday, Sally turns her tracked hours into invoices in Invoice Ninja. March's quote is there too, so she copies its rate into the new one.

detail.before: Invoices were built in FreshBooks, and the client list and every past quote lived there too.
detail.after: Invoice Ninja holds the clients, quotes, invoices and tracked time on the Core. Sally builds the month's invoices from what is already there.
steps: Open the client in Invoice Ninja
Add the month's tracked hours
Send the invoice
detail.fact: Invoice Ninja sends invoices and quotes and tracks expenses and time.

beats.capability: write and send newsletters to your own mailing list

popup.title: The mailing list stays at home
popup.body: Sally writes the practice's quarterly newsletter in Listmonk, and the subscriber list sits on the Core. Sending still goes through an outside mail provider.
popup.note: Delivery depends on the mail provider.

detail.before: The subscriber list lived in Mailchimp, along with the draft of every issue.
detail.after: Listmonk holds the subscriber list and the drafts on the Core. An outside mail provider sends each issue.
steps: Write the issue in Listmonk
Check the subscriber list
Send it through the mail provider
detail.fact: Listmonk writes and sends newsletters to your own mailing list.

beats.capability: write code in VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core

popup.title: One extension comes from outside
popup.body: John writes a cut-list script in Code Server at the workbench, and its folder sits on the Core. The one extension he adds comes from an outside registry.

detail.before: John coded in Cursor on the laptop, and the project folder lived on that one machine.
detail.after: Code Server gives John the editor in a browser tab. The editor and his files are on the Core, and extensions are fetched from an outside registry.
steps: Open the editor in a browser
Open the cut-list folder
Add the one extension he needs
detail.fact: Code Server runs VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core.

beats.capability: host private Git repositories, pull requests and issues on your Core

popup.title: Shelf-jig lands in Gitea
popup.body: John's last push today, a branch called shelf-jig, lands in Gitea on the Core, issues and pull requests beside it.

detail.before: John pushed his side projects to GitHub, with their issues and pull requests kept there too.
detail.after: Gitea hosts the repository on the Core, with its issues and pull requests beside it.
steps: Point the repository at Gitea
Push the shelf-jig branch
Open the pull request in Gitea
detail.fact: Gitea hosts private Git repositories, pull requests and issues on your Core.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Quill fills in the order form
popup.body: Quill opens the supplier's order form and fills it in for the shelf brackets John needs. John checks every field, then sends it himself.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

say.speaker: john
say.text: The order form is filled in. Please check the delivery address before you send it.

detail.before: Ordering hardware meant typing the same details into a supplier's form, field by field.
detail.after: Quill opens the supplier's page in its browser and fills in the form from what John typed. John reads every field and sends it himself.
steps: Type what he needs
Let Quill fill in the form
Read every field, then send it
detail.fact: OpenClaw is an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core.

beats.capability: back up your files with encryption before they leave your Core

popup.title: The spare lives in the garage
popup.body: Duplicati backs up the Core's folders, with encryption, to a local disk John has labelled. He keeps the disk in the garage cube storage, a floor away from the Core.

detail.before: Backups went to a Carbonite account, and the second copy lived with that service.
detail.after: Duplicati backs up the Core's folders with encryption to a local drive that John labels. The Core keeps the files, and the drive keeps the second copy.
steps: Plug the labelled drive into the Core
Set the backup in Duplicati
Carry the drive down to the garage
detail.fact: Duplicati backs up your files with encryption before they leave your Core.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: The game runs by the whiteboard
popup.body: Steve's game runs on the Core, beside the kitchen whiteboard. He signs in with his own Valve account, and the den TV shows it.
popup.note: Steam needs a Valve account. A Core may lack the graphics power a game wants.

detail.before: Steve played his Steam library through GeForce Now, with the session running somewhere else.
detail.after: Steam Headless runs Steam on the Core. The session shows in a browser on the den TV, and Valve still keeps the account and the library.
steps: Sign in with the Valve account
Open the session in the TV's browser
Pick a game from the library
detail.fact: Steam Headless runs Steam on your Core and plays it in a browser on a screen in the house.

beats.capability: edit audio in a browser tab: cut, fade, normalise and export

popup.title: The take loses its count-in
popup.body: The count-in comes off Steve's drum take in AudioMass, in a browser tab. The Core serves the editor, and he saves the file where he chooses.

detail.before: Steve trimmed his drum takes in TwistedWave.
detail.after: AudioMass opens in a browser tab served by the Core. Steve cuts the count-in, fades the end and saves the file where he chooses.
steps: Open the take in AudioMass
Cut the count-in and fade the end
Save the file where he chooses
detail.fact: AudioMass edits audio in a browser tab: cut, fade, normalise and export.

beats.capability: browse and share your photo library, with automatic tagging, without uploading it anywhere

popup.title: Same stone, same lavender, three summers
popup.body: Every August Jean takes one picture of the lavender from the same stepping stone. PhotoPrism lines the three summers up on the Core, and adding the next one uploads nothing.
popup.note: A photo library is not a backup. Keep the originals.

detail.before: The lavender pictures sat in iCloud Photos among everything else, and nobody had lined the summers up.
detail.after: PhotoPrism browses the family library on the Core, so Jean can set the three Augusts next to each other.
steps: Take the August picture from the stepping stone
Add it to the family library
Set the three summers side by side
detail.fact: PhotoPrism browses and shares your photo library, with automatic tagging, without uploading it anywhere.

popup.title: One Core, four different days
popup.body: A craft room, a workbench, a den and a shared bedroom, on one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your family's week, notes and homework can live on a Companion Core. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: garage-code uses Code Server, which has no QA screenshot: the owner has signed it off in content/story/reviewed.json (slug brennan-merrow, at garage-code, app-qa-screenshot). Not edited here.

Told in the v3 shape: 17 of 21 room beats are pair beats naming a service from content/story/services.json; the four pair-less ones are the Yuvomi whiteboard twin, Spellbook, the Companion Memory draft and Quill's order form.
Age rule 16: Jean (14) and Steve (16) use no chat model or agent in their own beats; Juniper and Quill work only for Sally and John, who approve every result.

Honest edges carried: Steam needs a Valve account; Pi-hole forwards unblocked lookups to the family's DNS provider; Listmonk sends through an outside mail provider; a photo library is not a backup, so John copies to a local drive.
Apps chosen to stay clear of the other two Brennan tours: only Yuvomi, Code Server, Steam Headless and the first-party agents are shared, as the cast plan assigns them.
